paragraphs: This passage is about a woman who loses nearly everything and still turns toward home. A famine sends Naomi's family to Moab (Ruth 1:1), and there her husband dies, and later her two sons die too (Ruth 1:3, 5). I think this part is heavy, friend, and the passage doesn't hurry past it. Then Naomi hears that the LORD has attended to His people by providing them with food, and she sets out for Judah (Ruth 1:6).

On the road, Naomi urges her daughters-in-law to go back to their mothers' homes, and she asks them why they would go with her (Ruth 1:8, 11). Orpah kisses her goodbye, but Ruth clings to her (Ruth 1:14). Then Ruth says, "your people will be my people, and your God will be my God." (Ruth 1:16). Naomi gives her the full speech, and Ruth stays stuck to her like a cookie that will NOT come off the pan.

When they reach Bethlehem, Naomi tells the women to call her Mara, and she says, "I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty." (Ruth 1:20, 21). She says what she feels out loud, and I think that's worth noticing. But Ruth is standing right beside her, and they arrive at the beginning of the barley harvest (Ruth 1:22). Hang on to your apron, friend, because this story is not over.
